comment: ATTACK STYLES. A style is a named STROKE PROGRAM: a windup that raises the blade into a stance, then a cut that drives it through the target line. It is fed to the SAME driver the player's mouse feeds (game/melee.h MeleeState, via StrokeSample), so an NPC swing is a motion a person could make and a fix to the feel is a fix to both. The player_* entries are the PLAYER'S discrete strikes (melee.controlMode 0), replayed through the same runner with the camera as the basis -- shorter windups because a click must feel owned, jitter 0 because a strike must go exactly where it was flicked. Hot-reloads on R alongside materials, behaviours, glyphs and items. The full schema, and the reasoning behind every field, is at the top of src/game/strokes.h.
notes: ANGLES ARE RADIANS in the mob's own facing basis: azimuth 0 is straight ahead and positive is the mob's right; elevation 0 is level. REACH is a fraction of the arm's own reach band, so a thrust is the same lunge on a long arm and a short one. TICKS are 30 Hz sim ticks -- a windup of 12 is 0.40 s of visible blade raise, which IS the telegraph (there is no UI indicator). The cut is CENTRED on the aim point: the windup lands at aim minus half the cut's own travel, so the blade passes through where it was aimed rather than starting there.
player_notes: The `player` block maps the FLICK at the attack press to a style: `dir` is a unit-ish direction in SCREEN space (+x right, +y DOWN, raw mouse), quantized by max dot product, so adding a sector is adding a line here. Mount & Blade's compass: right flick = cut from the right, up = overhead, down = thrust, up-right = the descending diagonal (it chambers at the right shoulder). A click with no flick (below melee.pickMinSpeed) alternates the two `neutralAlternate` entries.
playerUnarmed_notes: THE SAME COMPASS WITH NOTHING IN YOUR FIST (docs/PLAN_impact_unarmed.md §6). A SECOND map rather than a filter over the first, because the two are different SHAPES: a sword's compass has an overhead and a thrust where a fist's has a jab, a cross and a straight -- asking one set of sectors to mean both would make every punch a re-labelled sword cut. main.cpp picks between them on `meleeArmed`, and which FIST swings comes from the style's own `weapon` (fist.R / fist.L), through the same Mob::ArmForStyle an NPC uses.

styles.name: horizontal_l
styles.label: Backhand cut, across to weapon side

styles.name: overhead
styles.label: Overhead chop from a high guard

styles.name: thrust
styles.label: Rear chamber, then a straight thrust

styles.//: UNARMED, FROM HERE DOWN (docs/PLAN_impact_unarmed.md §5). Every one of these names a `weapon` -- a natural weapon on the creature's own rig (mob.h MobNaturalWeaponDef) rather than the default "held" -- and StyleUsable refuses it on a body that has not got that part, so a one-armed creature's repertoire shrinks by itself. The punches are all `fallback: true`: a duelist lists them beside its cuts, never draws one while a sword is in its fist, and throws nothing else once disarmed. The zombie's bites are NOT fallback, because biting is what it does. Numbers are starting points; the tuner's Attacks lane is where they get finished.
styles.name: punch_r
styles.label: Straight right
styles.//shape: A THRUST, NOT A SWING: a fist has no edge to sweep and no length past the wrist, so the damage has to come from the point going OUT. The reach pair is the thrust's own (-0.40 chamber, +0.80 drive) shortened a little, because an arm ending at a fist reaches less far than one ending at a sword and the band is resolved against the LIVE arm either way (StrokeReachIn). The windup is short -- 8 ticks, 0.27 s -- because a punch that telegraphs like an overhead chop is not a punch.

styles.name: punch_l
styles.label: Straight left
styles.//: The mirror, and the azimuth signs flip with it: azimuth is positive to the mob's RIGHT, so the off hand chambers left and crosses right.

styles.name: hook_r
styles.label: Right hook
styles.//shape: THE ONE PUNCH THAT IS A SWING. Azimuth-dominant and short-radius -- the fist travels around rather than out, which is why `reach` barely moves and the cut's azimuth is 1.1 rad. It reaches a voxel less far than the straights for the same reason a real hook does: the arm is bent through the whole of it.

styles.name: bite
styles.label: Bite
styles.//shape: THE JAWS ARE AN AIM EFFECTOR, not a chain: no rig puts the head in an IK chain, so the stroke ROTATES the head (and a share of the spine) until its forward lies along the bearing the driver commands -- Mob::ApplyStrikeAim lays StrokeAz/StrokeEl straight onto it. THE MOTION IS THEREFORE ALL IN THE ANGULAR CHANNELS. A first draft put it in `reach` (windup -0.35, cut +0.85) on the theory that a bite is a head thrusting forward, and that is what a head DOES -- but a part that can only point cannot translate, and the radial channel moved nothing at all. What carries the jaws to the throat is the BODY: `bite_lunge` leaps, and a standing bite is authored for a target already inside reach 7. So: rear back half a radian, then snap down and through by nearly one. The small `reach` pair is a token so the driver still has a radius to hold.
styles.//target: THE SAME WEIGHTS THE LUNGING BITE USES, and it needs them for the commoner case rather than the rarer one: a zombie already in reach -- crawling, cornered, or with its victim on the ground -- bites with THIS style, and without a table every one of those blows went to the chest (MobSystem::PickTargetLimb reads an absent table as `-1`, which BeginStroke turns into today's chest aim). The owner asked for bites that go for arms and torso too; that has to be true of the bite you actually meet.

styles.name: bite_lunge
styles.label: Lunge and bite
styles.//reach: FAR OUTSIDE THE ZOMBIE'S PROFILE REACH (9), which is the whole point: MobSystem::AttackReachOf hands the LONGEST usable style's reach to the AI, so the creature commits from three body-lengths out and the leap closes the rest. BeginStroke then refuses the punches at that distance, so the draw at 20 voxels can only come out as this.
styles.//lunge: FIRED AT THE START OF THE WINDUP, so the flight IS the telegraph -- there is no UI indicator and a zombie leaving the ground is the most readable warning in the game. `speed` is a CEILING in m/s, not a command: the magnitude is min(speed, (distance - the EFFECTOR's reach)/airTime), so the body arrives at biting distance instead of through the victim, and the same style is a long leap from far out and a hop from close in. `ticks` is what the AUTHOR is aiming the cut at (10 windup ticks, so the feet land about as the cut starts) and `rise` is what actually buys the time: a ballistic hop is airborne for 2*rise/gravity, so 1.5 m/s against 9.8 m/s^2 is 0.31 s = 9 ticks, which is where this number comes from. It must be non-zero or the launch lands on the tick after it left (mob.cpp UpdateFall's launch latch buys exactly one tick); measured at 1.1 the flight was 6 ticks and the leap fell 3 voxels short of the authored one.
styles.//target: WEIGHTS OVER LIMB TAGS, not names, so any rig that tags its parts answers it. Bites go for arms and torso too, not only the head -- the owner asked for that by name. Hands are in at 0.05 because a bitten-off hand is a thing that should happen occasionally and never look aimed at.
styles.//shape: Elevation-dominant like the standing bite above, and for the reason spelled out there: an aim effector POINTS, it does not translate, so a bite's motion has to live in the angular channels. A touch more of it than the standing one -- the body is arriving at speed and the head snaps through further.

styles.//: THE PLAYER'S UNARMED STRIKES. Shorter windups than the NPC punches for the same reason the player's sword styles are shorter than an NPC's: a click must feel owned. Jitter 0, so a strike goes exactly where it was flicked.
styles.name: player_punch_r
styles.label: Straight right
styles.//reach: A DEEPER CHAMBER AND A TICK MORE CUT THAN THE FIRST DRAFT. The driver moves a thrust by leaning the blade off a hand held at a fixed extension (melee.cpp's law of cosines), and a fist's whole blade is one voxel of knuckle -- so the radial channel has far less to work with than a sword's and a three-tick cut did not finish converging on it. Measured by npc-styles: commanded dr 0.92 voxels against its 1.0 floor, where the NPC punches (one more windup tick, one more cut tick) made 1.14.

styles.name: player_punch_thrust
styles.label: Two-handed drive
styles.//: The deepest chamber and the longest drive in the block, and almost no azimuth -- it is the punch you throw with your weight behind it. Down on the compass, where the sword's thrust lives, because it is the same gesture.
